answer: A Sybil attack fails when each identity costs an unrecoverable bond. Here an account must lock POA that is forfeited if it is proven sockpuppet-linked, so one operator pays the bond repeatedly. Like a reef that drowns hulls, the barrier charges every clone: a thousand identities mean a thousand forfeitable stakes, while honest miners post one. Increasing identity only adds bond to the pool, not power, so bots enter a garden they cannot flood cheaply. Verifiers trace the ferrous weight of stake, not the count of names.
